pains.title: One blended profit number hides which service line pays
pains.problem: Medical visits, surgery, pathology, cosmetic and retail behave differently, yet most books show a single profit and loss.

pains.title: Cosmetic cash and prepaid packages look like profit
pains.problem: Cosmetic revenue is paid up front, medical revenue arrives weeks later, and money for treatments not yet delivered gets counted as earned.

faq.q: How do I know if my dermatology practice is profitable by service line?
faq.a: Most practices run one blended profit and loss statement, which hides whether medical, surgical, cosmetic or lab work is carrying the practice. Lucid sets up your books by service line and gives you a monthly view reviewed by a CPA, so you see where margin comes from before you decide on hiring, equipment or a new location.

faq.q: Should I track cosmetic and medical revenue separately?
faq.a: Yes. Cosmetic is paid up front and medical is paid by insurers weeks later. Keeping them separate shows which side is truly profitable. Lucid keeps medical, cosmetic and retail revenue in separate accounts, reports revenue by service line and reconciles deposits with a rollforward for prepaid packages, and your CPA handles the tax treatment.

faq.q: How should my practice account for Botox, fillers and skincare products?
faq.a: Injectables and skincare products are booked as an asset on the balance sheet until they are used or sold, treatments and retail separately. That shows your true margin on each service and avoids surprises at tax time. Lucid reports profit by service line, and your Lucid tax team handles year end treatment.

faq.q: How do I get my books ready if a private equity firm calls?
faq.a: Buyers rebuild your earnings from your books, so unreconciled records and mixed personal expenses slow or lower an offer. Lucid keeps your books reconciled and your service lines separate, and handles intercompany reconciliation with a management company. Your attorney handles the deal structure.

faq.q: Our insurance payments are slow and we have many denials. How can accounting help?
faq.a: Your biller handles the claims. Lucid gives you the financial view: payer mix tracking and a cash forecast that shows what slow payment means for next month's cash.
